### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx`  _(via INVALID_FILTER (literal, a string literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via INVALID_FILTER (literal, a string literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx`  _(via INVALID_FILTER (literal, a string literal on a changed line))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via INVALID_FILTER (literal, a string literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via INVALID_FILTER (literal, a string literal on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f3b428335bb9e1efdf6896afdc9cb8c60179c2fb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b5a0ac8e09b65b4d2020cc43d5688a0a85ef7414` — the merge of head `812a5bf56595defe827cd27856f577e3699468ab` into base `f3b428335bb9e1efdf6896afdc9cb8c60179c2fb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b5a0ac8e09b65b4d2020cc43d5688a0a85ef7414 && git checkout b5a0ac8e09b65b4d2020cc43d5688a0a85ef7414
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f3b428335bb9e1efdf6896afdc9cb8c60179c2fb 812a5bf56595defe827cd27856f577e3699468ab && git checkout -B drift-repro f3b428335bb9e1efdf6896afdc9cb8c60179c2fb && git merge --no-ff 812a5bf56595defe827cd27856f577e3699468ab

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f3b428335bb9e1efdf6896afdc9cb8c60179c2fb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f3b428335bb9e1efdf6896afdc9cb8c60179c2fb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

80/80 at-tier stamps (control: an `os-dev` round in this same session reads 209/209 `claude-opus-5`)
Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `812a5bf56595defe827cd27856f577e3699468ab`

### ① Derived judgments

ACCEPT SET (measured on the head tree and my build of it; every claim falsifiable from the commands above):

1. isRefusedTextComparand answers true for exactly the two REJECTION rows FILTER_TEXT_CASES declares for the case-insensitive-contains operator (the empty string at L447, the number 42 at L455) and false for every other comparand in the 24-case table, for the three retired-operator rejections (comparands 'ac.*', '^acme', 'i'), and for all 9 FILTER_TEXT_ROWS names. RIGHT. Nothing on origin/main calls it (0 hits, positive control 5 files on the PR ref), so no existing acceptance set moves; the door is additive.
2. It answers true for undefined (typeof undefined is not 'string') and the JSDoc says so and assigns the absence carve-out to the caller. RIGHT, and consistent with the reference consumer, which tests rule.value for undefined before the door.
3. The three function bodies are byte-identical to objectui 55f39ee9 blob c29782139426 (160/116/929 bytes each, only the export modifier differs). RIGHT: the fence "port the bytes, do not reword" is satisfied.
4. The reason interpolates the arriving operator verbatim and its templates carry no literal dollar sign, so for an arriving infix 'icontains' the reason contains 'icontains' and cannot contain '$icontains' (measured: contained=false for both rows; hasDollar=false). RIGHT per the card's own definition of function 2 ("the spelling that ARRIVED, never a canonical substitute"); see clause 2 below.
5. No text the PR ships asserts a false runtime behaviour. Checked and held: the undefined answer; JSON.stringify throwing on BigInt and on a cyclic object and returning undefined for undefined and a symbol (node); both rows carry code INVALID_FILTER and mustMention ['$icontains']; the rows exist since #5701 (commit 85d95e7d92, 2026-08-06); INVALID_FILTER is in the ADR-0112 catalog (errors.zod.ts:64); the sibling positive operators have no rejection row (0 each); the retired-operator rows have ordinary non-empty string comparands; three objectui seats read the reason unchanged and the infix seat names the $ twin in its own tail; the table carries 24 cases and 5 rejections; the cited filter-text-conformance.test.ts exists.

PUBLIC SURFACE:

6. Exactly two symbols become importable that were not before, on the './data' entry only: set-diff of the built artifact's runtime export names against origin/main's api-surface/data.json is exactly isRefusedTextComparand and textComparandRefusalReason, identical on dist/data/index.mjs, dist/data/index.js and both browser twins; both are declared in dist/data/index.d.mts and .d.ts. RIGHT.
7. describeComparand is not importable from any shipped entry (absent from both type files, 'in' test false on all four runtime files; present only as an internal body in the js bundles). The two-symbol claim on the card, the PR and the changeset is TRUE of the artifact, not just the source. RIGHT.
8. The root entry is unchanged: dist/index.mjs exports neither symbol, and the control data-only symbol isAcceptedFilterComparand is also absent at root, so leaving api-surface/root.json untouched is correct. RIGHT.
9. api-surface/data.json and export-origins/data.json are exactly what the generators emit from the built artifact: check:api-surface exit 0, check:export-origins exit 0, check:generated reports all 15 artifacts up to date with a clean tree. RIGHT.
10. Package hygiene at head: typecheck exit 0 including check:test-typecheck with both new files in the tsconfig.test.json program; eslint 0 on the three TS files; 79 pins pass across the new test and the table's own test. check:cross-package-test-inputs is red in a built tree but names only packages/cli's e2e test descending into packages/spec/dist (0 mentions of any PR file; the PR touches neither the cli test nor the gate) — pre-existing, correctly reported as out of scope, not a defect of this diff.

ACCEPTANCE CLAUSES, one by one:

- Clause 1 (pin driving every case; "each REJECTION case answers true, each FILTER_TEXT_ROWS comparand answers false"). The pin exists (24 per-case assertions, a whole-table set assertion, all 9 stored names). As WRITTEN the clause is falsified: 3 of the 5 REJECTION cases answer FALSE, because they are refused for a retired OPERATOR and their comparands are ordinary strings. The card's own item 1 ("true exactly for the two REJECTION rows ... for the case-insensitive-contains operator") and ruling D scope the predicate to that operator, so the resolution is to CORRECT THE CLAUSE to "each REJECTION case for the icontains operator answers true; every other comparand in the table answers false", not to change the diff. The PR already pins that reading in both directions ("answers FALSE for the RETIRED-operator rejections"). The dev did not raise this one; it is recorded here.
- Clause 2 (reason for '' and a non-string contains each case's mustMention tokens for BOTH arriving spellings). Falsified for the infix spelling, measured: contained=false for both rows when the operator arrives as 'icontains'. Resolution: correct the clause, see ③. The diff is right.
- Clause 3 (Clause-②: yes; two new symbols; changeset minor; carrier at claim). SATISFIED: carrier on card and PR, the PR body carries the Clause-② line, two symbols measured on the artifact, changeset minor (②).
- Clause 4 (measure whether a repo face is a literal copy; fold if so, else report). SATISFIED by measurement: formula answers false in a positive arm (not a refusal); the five throwing faces share the one-line discrimination but each throws its own differently-worded icontainsComparandError; the ported reason sentence has 0 hits in this repo (controls non-zero). No literal copy of predicate-plus-reason; report-and-leave is correct.
- Fences: no objectui file in the 6-path diff; errors.zod.ts untouched (no new code); content/docs/releases untouched. All HELD.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/18113-icontains-text-comparand-refusal.md`, frontmatter: "@objectstack/spec": minor. The diff adds two exports and removes or narrows nothing (api-surface diff 2 added, 0 removed; check:api-surface reports the surface unchanged against the committed snapshot; export-origins 5165 exports resolve as recorded; runtime set-diff exactly two names). @objectstack/spec is public at 17.4.0 and ships dist. A declared Clause-② yes takes at least minor (AGENTS.md post-task step 3; check-changeset-no-major encodes the same rule; Check Changeset ran green twice at this head). minor MATCHES the diff: patch would be refused, major is unwarranted. The fixed group bumps its members together, which is a config consequence and not a misdeclaration.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev raised one flag in open_questions: acceptance clause 2 asks the reason to contain mustMention for BOTH arriving spellings, and for the infix 'icontains' it cannot; options A (keep the ported bytes; the face names the $ twin), B (reword to always name $icontains), C (widen mustMention on the two rows).

Answer: A, re-derived on the table rather than on the dev's recommendation. (i) The two mustMention rows are both written in the $ dialect (filters { name: { $icontains: '' } } and { name: { $icontains: 42 } }); the table's single infix-spelled case is a rows case, not a rejection. mustMention is therefore a per-row requirement on a refusal of THAT row's filter, which always arrives as $icontains; the table imposes nothing on an infix arrival, and clause 2's "BOTH arriving spellings" over-extends the table. (ii) The reason's templates contain no literal dollar sign, so for 'icontains' the output has none; the clause is unsatisfiable by the bytes the card itself fences. (iii) B breaks the card's own ⛔ do-not-reword fence and ruling D's "its reason text", contradicts the card's definition of function 2 (never a canonical substitute), and would change bytes three shipped objectui seats emit today. (iv) C edits published conformance data outside this card's face and does not even satisfy the clause: ['$icontains','icontains'] still leaves the infix reason without '$icontains', and ['icontains'] alone weakens every enrolled backend's requirement by accepting a $-dialect refusal that drops the sigil. Resolution: keep the diff; the seat corrects clause 2 to read "for the $icontains arrival the reason contains every mustMention token; for the icontains arrival it names the arriving spelling and the face serving that vocabulary names the $ twin in its envelope" — which is exactly what the PR pins in both directions. Not escalated: the table's own rows settle it at review level.

No other flag was raised. The three out_of_scope_findings are findings, not flags; the first (build-state-dependent check:cross-package-test-inputs) reproduced in my clone as described and is not a verdict input on this PR.
